notes.title: Devlog - Introverts
notes.content:
[h1]Introverts[/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39224458/77fe665f1da1b464edce8e5690684cb7ac254a24.png[/img]

Hello there, Introverts! In today’s Devlog we would like to talk about you… Well, Introverts! We will reveal our ideas and intentions from the beginning of our development phase.

The Introvert is a bit of a blank slate, because they are, well, you! They’re a typical teenager who loves their friends but also appreciates some quiet time to recharge their batteries. Unfortunately for the introvert, they live in a city that loves small talk. A quiet person, the introvert expresses themselves through fashion, decorating their room, and mostly replies in emojis. However, with that said, the introvert isn’t mute, and has several conversation segments in the game.

The introvert being the protagonist felt natural to a platformer, as we kinda had two ways we could’ve gone: a Pokemon-style turn-based battle collector where you collect introverts and force them to talk to each other, or this. This made sense to make first, but hopefully, we’ll get to do the other one in the future! 

Your friends are a mix of introverts and extroverts! You can tell based on whether their eyes or their mouths are obscured. Very few characters in the game are ambiverts - a mix of both - and therefore have both eyes and their mouth visible! 

We based the friendship group off our own friends and experiences when we were in high school, fed through the blender of the cartoons we grew up with. We tried to avoid the typical “high school stereotypes” you see in many TV shows. So, our gang of friends aren’t allergic to parties but don’t go to a new one every week. They aren’t criminals but can commit the occasional bending of the law. They’re more into video games than alcohol, but they’re teenagers. 

We wanted to avoid making them too “adult,” while also avoiding making them too “childlike.” 

Don’t Stare’s story is also pretty self-contained. If we expand the story, there’s a chance we’d introduce some new characters, given that they fit with what we wanna do, of course! 

Thank you for your time, we hope that you have a lot of fun learning about our inspiration for the game!

See you in the next Devlog!

notes.title: Devlog - Extroverts
notes.content:
[h1]Extroverts[/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39224458/9d575b38954155e440123d68f948facdf262b95f.png[/img]

Hello there Introverts! In today’s Devlog we would like to talk about extroverts, which you will need to avoid if you want to beat the game! We hope this will give you some insight into our intentions when creating the “villain” characters.

Our main idea was to create an introverted character that would avoid extroverts! It was really important for us from the start to avoid making the extroverts antagonistic or “villains,” as we didn’t want to be more mean-spirited than intended. Our extroverts are not evil - just different.

Some extrovert abilities were designed to be beneficial to the player, while some were designed to be beneficial/detrimental depending on the situation, and based on whether the player has eye contact or not. A few extroverts were designed to be purely a detrimental obstacle. 

The extroverts were created from two sources - what the game needs, and what we think would be funny. Some extroverts started first as a purely mechanical challenge, with no real contextualization as a particular character or behavior. In those cases, we’d try to contextualize the challenge as a specific extrovert after prototyping the ability thoroughly.

In other cases, the idea of the extrovert came to us in a “complete” state, where both the mechanical behavior and the extrovert’s appearance, animations, etc. were clear from the start. The Salesman and his teleport ability was one of those cases. 

We wanted to try and make most of the extroverts funny and unexpected, and as such, our extroverts usually have “surprising” abilities that still fit within the stereotype they fill.

It is also worth mentioning that your character regains social battery by petting animals in the levels, who also function as checkpoints!

Fun fact - If you pay attention to the faces of the characters in the game, you’ll find a common thread: the introverts have their mouths hidden, while the extroverts have their eyes hidden. A few characters are ambiverts (both introverted and extroverted), and have both visible eyes and mouths.

Thank you for your time, we hope that you like the next steps in the development of our game!

See you in the next Devlog!

notes.title: Devlog - Inspiration for the Game
notes.content:
[h1]Inspiration for the Game[/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39224458/123e9d8b7130a033d6ee3d6b0d0f664afac6324a.png[/img]

Hello there Introverts! In today’s Devlog we would like to talk about our Inspiration for the game! We will reveal our ideas and thoughts from the beginning of our development phase.

The inspiration came from the fact that extroverts and introverts are different, and we wanted to do something that celebrated that difference!

The introvert being the protagonist felt natural to a platformer, as we kinda had two ways we could’ve gone: a Pokemon-style turn-based battle collector where you collect introverts and force them to talk to each other, or this. This made sense to make first, but hopefully, we’ll get to do the other one in the future!

We wanted to create a funny game where you laugh with each other, not at others. It was important for us that the introverts, and the extroverts, were equal amounts of silly in their own ways. During development, we intentionally avoided words like “enemies,” in regards to the extroverts, as they’re not your enemy - they just like talking to people!

For us, the humor lies in the ridiculous lengths the introvert goes to avoid conversations with people, and the wild abilities of the extroverts. Obviously, the introvert will feel a bit more sympathetic, being the main character, but we’ve tried to dish out the silliness as even-handedly as we could! 

In terms of graphics - We aimed to evoke the nostalgic feeling of Saturday mornings when we spent all our time watching cartoons. The idea was to create an experience where players could relieve those carefree moments with the sense of a new adventure in each chapter. We also were super happy to be able to get inspiration from the amazing artists who worked on the 90s animated shows. 

About the story - We always knew we wanted to do a story about differences, and learning to understand and celebrate those differences. As stated, we wanted to create something that laughed with introverts and extroverts, not at anyone in particular. 

With the “Saturday morning cartoon show” angle developing in the art style, it began bleeding into how we were thinking about the game as a whole. Since the game is all about differences, and learning to accept and celebrate those differences, we wanted to give you friends with their own differences and struggles, who could work as anchoring points for our themes. 

We also wanted to do something that reminded us of being idiots in high school and wanted to try and capture that within the “cartoon show” boundaries we’d set for ourselves. We didn’t want to portray a party-filled, “adult” idealization of teenager-dom, but we also didn’t want to make them needlessly toothless. So, our characters commit petty crimes, joke about firebombing stuff, and mostly just hang out and play video games. 

Thank you for your time, we hope that you have a lot of fun learning about our inspiration for the game!

See you in the next Devlog!

notes.title: Devlog - Maps Design
notes.content:
[h1]Maps Design[/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39224458/f8acb478b8d292563a644a7940ea0e1ccfccf288.png[/img]

Hello there Introverts! In today’s Devlog we would like to talk about Map Design. We hope it will give you some insight into our intentions when creating one and how we feel about map design.

Don’t Stare is a narrative game, so each level is built around the narrative we want to tell. Many of our spaces are “normal” spaces as mentioned, so we have a lot of city environments - but each environment is handcrafted. With that said, there’s a limit to how many assets and stuff we can make, so obviously you’re going to see the same Scandinavian post-modern terror building more than a few times.

When designing levels for Don’t Stare, the process usually starts with finding a central challenge of sorts, which is tied to a specific “skill theme.” So, if we want to test players’ timing skills, we’ll create a central challenge that is tied to that - like jumping on a moving platform at the right time. Then, we “evolve” the challenge by introducing new things, and “expand” the challenge by making it a bit harder - making the platform smaller, or making you have to jump from a balloon that is about to pop! 

By evolving and expanding the central challenge into new challenges, our levels feel a bit more cohesive… though be advised, some levels are designed to just be chaotic to simulate the chaos of extrovert overload in public! 

Generally, each level has a particular mechanic or combination of mechanics, that we want you to master and play around with. 

In terms of the buildings and spaces we wanted to make, we wanted to create a “global city” that was a mix of all the different places our team’s from, and then some! We didn’t want any of our levels to feel like they’re from a particular continent or country, instead being something anybody, anywhere, can find something that feels like home.

There are 5 “warm up” levels, and 49 “RealTM” levels. There are also 5 epilogue levels, but you just talk to people in those, lmao. Our levels are split into five “zones,” which in Don’t Stare, are the months of your school semester! Each zone focuses on something different from the other. 

The core inspiration is that I am a fast walker, and a very grumpy dude, so when people get in my way in public, I wish I could parkour over them! We wanted to set each level in a “normal” space, with many of our levels being spaces in between spaces - going to school, concerts, or the café. 

Most maps either introduce a new gimmick, or a new extrovert or find new ways to combine gimmicks and extroverts! I’m sure you might find some challenges that are similar to each other (if not almost identical lmao) but we were fortunate to have a lot of extroverts and gimmicks to play with in making our levels, allowing us to serve something new pretty often!

There are collectibles in the levels themselves, where you’ll find stuff for your character, and for your room. You’ll have to look for them, tho - no collectible is awarded merely for completing the level!

Thank you for your time, we hope that you like the next steps in the development of our game!

See you in the next Devlog!

notes.title: The 2023 Rewind!
notes.content:
[h1][b]Hello, Introverts![/b][/h1]

We are here today to let you know about our work during 2023! It was a crazy year for us, we have made a lot of changes and additions. We hope you will have a lot of fun reviewing all of them with us!

[b][h2]Let's jump into it![/h2][/b]

[h3][b]Overall State[/b][/h3]

We have made significant progress in all of the game aspects, we have listed the most important ones!

[list]
[*] Completed all the features for the game
[*] Completed a bunch of extroverts, gimmicks, and levels for the game
[*] Created a host of accessibility features, with more planned
[/list]

[h3][b]Extroverts[/b][/h3]

The Extroverst are the main antagonists in our game, and we are taking great care of creating them. They not only have a unique look but also [b]special abilities[/b]! Always be ready with a good strategy when facing those people!

[list]
[*]We’ve created [b]18 new extroverts[/b] for you, and counting!!
[*] Each extrovert has their [b]own special abilities[/b], usually triggered by eye contact or by breaking eye contact!
[*] Here we put a few that we like to show off
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39224458/d8eb0f5ce24241a0ea79832b84d6a00a66467971.gif[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39224458/1c72f967354d67187e09eec57bfa89d22ab1c798.gif[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39224458/cc92910643a939ae4155cbb826d819fb70d646d1.gif[/img]

[h3][b]Game Developer’s Conference[/b][/h3]

This year, we were able to go to our very first Game Developer’s Conference in San Francisco! We had a blast, met lots of awesome people, and we were able to show off the game at various events around town. Thanks so much to everyone who let us show the game, and thank you to everyone who played it, gave feedback, and reiterated that yes, this IS literally their life!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39224458/3c88e609e2356a08b91369b2ad4ba95b5252f20b.jpg[/img]

[h3][b]Room Customization[/b][/h3]

Being an introvert means your room is your [b]sanctuary[/b], so we wanted to make sure you can customize it to your heart’s content!

[list]
[*] This year, we put the finishing touches on our room customization feature.
[*] We created a whole list of different room themes, and can’t wait to see how you’ll mix and match them!
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39224458/a920e31dc356907baab0fabf550aa856c445930f.gif[/img]

[h3][b]Character Customization[/b][/h3]

We want to give you the ability to express yourself through your clothes as well!

[list]
[*] We completed our character customization feature, and created a whole host of hoodies, trousers, skirts, boots, backpacks, and more for you!
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39224458/49732bf782c46707b1709bae9351a83b1c585971.gif[/img]

[h3][b]Accessibility[/b][/h3]

It’s important for us that anyone can play Don’t Stare, so, we’ve added a bunch of accessibility features:

[list]
[*] Adjustable values for magnet zones, damage values, etc.
[*] Auto health recovery
[*] Bouncy pits, so if you’re about to fall out of the level, you’ll simply bounce back up again!
[*] Fully remappable controls!
[*] Color blind mode 
[*] Dyslexia font
[*] Font size
[*] Adjustable brightness, contrast, and saturation values!
[/list]

[h3][b]Teasing for the Future[/b][/h3]

In the following year, we would like to move forward with our game development, implementing the following content:

[list]
[*] More extroverts!
[*] More gimmicks!
[*] More levels!
[*] We also have some fun features to show off soon - two new additions that make the extroverts even scarier than before!
[*] Release? 👀
[/list]

We want to thank you all for your support during the development phase. If you would like to know more about the game, feel free to join our [url=https://discord.gg/wXjtfDY][b]Discord Server![/b][/url]

[i][b]~Ascended Team[/b][/i]

notes.title: Dev Update 2.0 - Summer Edition!
notes.content:
Hello and welcome to the second Dev Update for Don't Stare, our indie platformer that follows the adventures of an introvert on a quest for peace and tranquility, while on the run from loud-mouthed but good natured extroverts!

It is the height of summer and we are sweating buckets! Not on account of the weather, but rather because of the hot updates that we have released into the game. 

Here is what we have been working on for the past scorching month! 

[b]Room customization feature[/b]

One of the key traits of introverts is their creativity. One of the main conduits for this creativity in Don't Stare will be our room customization feature which will allow you to design, furnish and decorate your very own fortress of solitude, away from the hustle and the bustle of the outside world. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39224458/fbc9fe40050c25ddeb4e80aba1ae828a02095cfe.jpg[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39224458/30a68fef67f8c88c3c81a06c6f518f1be5a2862d.jpg[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39224458/9c3d1252159bb8574912262865dc1ee0bc69e340.jpg[/img]

Items  can be collected through gameplay and are separated by room set. Each item is interchangeable and you can mix and match to find the perfect tapestry of your seclusion. We are now up to[b] 10 different room sets[/b], some of which you may have  noticed if you follow us on [url=https://linktr.ee/dontstaregame]social media[/url]! 

On the programming side, the collection and decoration features themselves are done, currently being tested. Good things come to those who wait, and we literally cannot wait to see our players unleash their inner interior designer! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39224458/e8e838c5be6349eb164d2068f9795c8ed39efcb5.jpg[/img]

[b]New extrovert characters[/b]

The roster of extrovert characters that want to talk your ear off is expanding and we are very excited that the Bois are finally in the game! This gym-bro trio might seem intimidating at a first glance, but when benching their friend, they can actually function as a platform, allowing the player to jump even higher and reach places normally out of their reach. 

There are[b] four other extrovert characters[/b] that we are currently working on, which we may reveal in the near future. 

Follow us on social media to be among the first to find out!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39224458/a192d3c9a283cd6006ab6b2ba7f72141fd38972f.png[/img]
[b]
Parkour System[/b]

Our introverted main character is athletic as they come, using their high-powered legs to leap out of the way of incoming smalltalk. But did you know that not all jumping schemes are created equal. 
We are very happy to have reached the milestone of marking our parkour system as complete this past month. 

What is the parkour system? It is an optional movement mechanic that allows you to use parkour items in the world to maneuver faster! It allows you to run up walls, bounce off objects, and balance-run along railings and other such objects. 

No level requires Parkour to finish it, and Parkour routes are usually more dangerous than the normal route, but it'll let you move through the level faster.

[b]Other additions and improvements:[/b]
[list]
[*] We have added several level hazards and objects, like gusts of wind that move your character, a hiding feature that lets you avoid extroverts, and more!
[*] We are currently working on implementing cut scenes and cinematics.
[*] Talking animations for the main character's friends are ready.[/list]

That is it for this dev update. Thank you for reading and [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1456220/Dont_Stare/]do not forget to wishlist[/url] if you have not already!

notes.title: Dev Update 1.0
notes.content:
Hello there!

If you are reading this then you’ve found your way to our Steam page and may have some interest in our little project, or maybe you wound up here by the sheer randomness of life. 

Either way, you are awesome and welcomed!  

Originally announced in 2020, Don’t Stare is currently in development and we hope to release it soon. With this first update, and more to follow, our aim is to chronicle our dev-adventures in the quest to bring this title to the masses.

Without further ado, here’s what we have been up to!

[b]We had the opportunity to run a playtest or two in the last 2 years, and the feedback we collected was invaluable! [/b] Following that process, we are currently working on a [b]FTUE tutorial[/b] to help future users get started in the game and learn the ropes. 

Don’t Stare is not the most complicated game out there, but we know how important it is to make our game accessible to all players.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39224458/d52769a6ff089f3ace3a78ab658d6961b30e8777.jpg[/img]

On the art front, our team has been busy creating more assets than ever before. [b]We have added new levels with themes such as a coffee shop, grocery store and subway.[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39224458/aa92b0468ce1fd869e9d633ca792b443cfe69f8d.jpg[/img]

[b]We've also introduced new characters, including the Bois, Mom and Dad with the baby, and the Old Man. [/b]

The [b]main character's friends[/b] are now also in the game, and we can’t wait for you to meet them!
